content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper suggests low-complexity neural decoding of binary algebraic codes based on the layered min-sum algorithm. The proposed algorithm is shown to have low complexity by 1) achieving a better error correction performance for a given number of iterations and 2) requiring a fewer number of weights for neural decoders. The paper also combines the mRRD with the proposed decoding method, which achieves near-ML performances for short codes.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 
- The proposed method performs well with some specific settings -- short length.

Weaknesses:
- From my understanding, this paper simply applies neural networks for decoding algebraic codes. Although it shows an improvement in error-correcting performance and complexity from the evaluation results, I'm not quite sure whether the ICLR community is the best audience for this paper. I'd instead recommend somewhere in the IEEE communications society; the paper mainly discusses a very high-level summary of the method and then the evaluation results primarily based on the curves of BER vs E_b/N_o. It'd be good if we had some more relevant explanation, e.g., how to train the proposed neural decoder in a little more detail.
- In 5. Simulation results, this paper only contains results using relatively short codes. What if we increase the length -- to moderate/long? It'd be good if this paper could contain any insights into why the proposed method wouldn't work with larger codes.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity/Quality: This paper reads well; it contains a fair amount of introduction to previous studies.
Novelty: From my understanding, it's a variant of a previous method resulting in a better performance.
Reproducibility: I believe this paper is reproducible based on Monte Carlo simulations.
content.summary_of_the_review: It's clear what this paper achieves. However, it's not entirely clear to me what this paper significantly contributes to the machine-learning community as mentioned above.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a neural min-sum decoder for algebraic codes such as BCH and QR codes. By reducing the number of training weights and using a cyclic redundant parity-check matrix, the decoder outperforms baseline algorithms with lower computational complexity. In addition, they also combine the neural decoder and mRRD algorithms showing that its computational cost is lower than an existing list decoder.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
*Strength 

The decoder successfully improves decoding performance and reduces computational complexity compared to existing algorithms.

*Weakness

1. Novelty of the proposed architecture

1-a. The proposed neural mRDD seems to contain three new features; a neural layered min-sum decoder, the use of a cyclic redundant parity-check matrix, and an mRDD algorithm. However, each feature does not sounds new. Especially, a neural layered min-sum decoder is a natural concept and has been proposed (see e.g. [1]). Thus, the only contribution of this paper seems to propose a combination of those features. As stated after, however, the contribution is only reported numerically and no theoretical contribution exists in this paper.

[1] N. Shah and Y. Vasavada, "Neural Layered Decoding of 5G LDPC Codes," in IEEE Communications Letters, vol. 25, no. 11, pp. 3590-3593, Nov. 2021, doi: 10.1109/LCOMM.2021.3113610.

1-b. The authors claim a contribution that they also propose an ML simulation-based algorithm using linear and integer programming. However, the proposed algorithm seems nearly ML decoder and inexact as far as I read Appendix C.

2. No theoretical discussions

Obviously, this paper contains no theoretical discussions about the performance of the proposed decoders. As a reader, it is hard to understand why the authors should combine three features and it works well numerically. After careful reading, I noticed that a cyclic redundant parity-check matrix might control the schedules of neural min-sum decoding and that mRDD might randomly search the order of decoding. However, I consider that the authors need to theoretically explain the role and aim of each component carefully. 

3. Lack of numerical simulations

In terms of numerical results, I consider that there are rooms to improve. For example, authors are expected to compare the neural layered min-sum decoder to a standard neural min-sum decoder containing full of training weights to show the performance degradation of the proposed decoder. This will show not only the performance degradation but also the certification of whether the layered structure is allowed in terms of decoding performance.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Judging from carefully reading the paper and the above analysis, I need to consider that the contributions and novelty of this paper are below the conference criterion, unfortunately. 

As for reproducibility, the authors need to note the learning settings of the proposed neural decoders. The current paper has no information on learning conditions.
content.summary_of_the_review: Although the proposed algorithms look numerically good, the paper needs to be revised largely in terms of claiming contributions, theoretical analyses, and reproducibility. I thus consider that this paper is below the criterion of this conference.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a novel neural-network-based decoder for binary algebraic codes (more specifically, BCH and QR codes). While a number of related works has focused on creating neural network counterparts of BP algorithms, here the neural network is based on the layered min-sum decoder. In order to further improve the performance and approach the ML decoder, the authors also incorporate the mRRD decoder which combines multiple permutations of the received message. The simulation results compare the proposed method with (i) the layered min-sum algorithm, (ii) the cyclically equivariant BP decoder of Chen & Ye (2021), and (iii) ML decoding.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

(1) Using min-sum instead of BP is a natural idea, hence developing a neural network counterpart of the layered min-sum algorithm has the potential to provide significant gains.

(2) The simulation results show a noticeable improvement w.r.t. the original layered min-sum algorithm. Furthermore, the number of iterations needed to achieve ML performance is greatly reduced in comparison with the list decoder of Chen & Ye (2021).


Weaknesses:

The key weakness of the current version of the paper is in its numerical results, which are still somewhat preliminary.
 
(1) The block lengths considered are too small to be practical (63 for BCH and {47, 71} for QR). Showing a reduction in the number of iterations of 90% is interesting, but this should be the basis to actually scale the algorithm to larger block lengths. As a matter of fact, in (Chen & Ye, 2021) the authors consider codes of block length up to 127. If the authors are able to show that their method scales as well, this would add significant value to the contribution.

(2) When comparing with CEBP, the most impressive numerical results are improvements between 0.29 and 0.37 dB observed only for low target BER (10^(-5)). Furthermore, in order to report such a gain for BCH(63, 45, 7), the authors have to resort to the mRRD version of their algorithm which is compared to the list decoder of (Chen & Ye, 2021) with a similar complexity. In fact, Figure 4(a) displays essentially the same performance between CEBP and NLMS. In order to make a stronger point, the authors should test more codes and show improvements for a wider range of settings. As mentioned above, being able to scale to larger lengths would be the most important direction.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The idea is novel, but the numerical results not entirely convincing.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper pursues the very natural idea of implementing a neural network version of the layered min-sum decoder. This is an interesting direction that is definitely worth pursuing. However, the numerical results (in their current stage) are not fully convincing and the improvement over the state of the art (represented by the CEBP approach of (Chen & Ye, 2021)) remains a bit marginal.

content.title: Neural Layered Min-sum Decoders for Algebraic Codes
content.abstract: In this article, we propose low-complexity neural network decoders based on the layered min-sum algorithm to decode binary algebraic codes. By generalizing the layered min-sum algorithm to its neural network counterpart, the number of iterations required for convergence is reduced. Consequently, the number of network weights decreases while retaining a good error correction performance. The Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH) codes and quadratic residue (QR) codes are selected as two exemplary binary algebraic codes. Simulation results show that the proposed decoders achieve superior performance with less computational complexity,  compared with the decoders proposed by Chen & Ye (2021). Further, a neural decoder incorporating the modified random redundant decoding (mRRD) algorithm is investigated to approach the performance of maximum-likelihood (ML) decoding for some short codes.
